steps.text: Whisk sugar, soy sauce, water, onion powder, and ground ginger together in a medium saucepan over high heat. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature, 20 to 30 minutes. Whisk in lemon juice and chili paste.

raw_recipe.headline: Korean BBQ Chicken Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This Korean BBQ chicken recipe features a sweet, salty, and spicy marinade perfect for any cut of chicken, and as a basting sauce when grilling.
raw_recipe.name: Korean BBQ Chicken Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk sugar, soy sauce, water, onion powder, and ground ginger together in a medium saucepan over high heat. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature, 20 to 30 minutes. Whisk in lemon juice and chili paste.

review.reviewBody: This was awesome. I tweaked it a bit by adding 1 tsp minced garlic and I subst. red pepper flakes (1 heaping tsp)for the paste. I found this recipe at the last minute so I didnt marinate. I used 10 chicken tenderloins, removed the tendons, fat, etc, and cut into bite sized pieces. I then put the chicken in a 9x13 pan and poured enough of the marinade to cover chicken. I covered with foil and baked at 350 for 35 min. stirring halfway through to make sure chicken was covered evenly with sauce. I reduced the remaining marinade in a saucepan, added a bit more water and thickened with cornstarch. When Chicken was done, I added some steamed broccoli florets and the thickened sauce right to the 9x13 pan and tossed to coat, served over jasmine rice. NO leftovers in my house, My husband ate 3 helpings! Even my 2 and 3 year olds ate it up! Definitely a keeper!

I served chicken with this marinade to my Korean parents for dinner. My mom, who said she wasn't hungry before we started eating, ended up going back for seconds and exclaimed that it was delicious. The only changes I made was to decrease the sugar by 1/3 C(trying to make it healthier), and add minced garlic and a touch of sesame oil. Gotta have garlic when you're making Korean!

This is such a great marinade and sauce! I used it for boneless skinless chicken thighs, which we grilled. I took some of the other reviewers’ recommendations to turn the marinade into a sauce for the chicken after it was done marinating. I simmered the marinade with some minced garlic and cornstarch to reduce a little and thicken, then glazed the chicken with it after it was done grilling. The sauce was so good that I saved the leftover sauce to use again.
The marinade came out delicious! I put all the ingredients together then boiled & simmered. I also used fresh onion including the the greens and 3 cloves of garlic, lime instead of lemon.
I did not have hot chili paste so I added siracha, did not boil but marinated overnight. Turned out great.
I cut the amount of sugar in half and it still seemed a little too sweet. May cut back a little more the next time and increase the hot chili paste.

Very tasty marinade and not overpowering. I searched for this recipe because I was given a free bag of Korean breading for an online review of their version of fried BBQ chicken. After it was sent to me, the directions called for their version of bagged marinade which was not part of the deal (LOL). And so I made this following the instructions to a tee but adding minced garlic, sesame seeds, and sesame oil as suggested in other reviews. It did indeed imbue the chicken parts with a great flavor and although calling for the chili paste which I had on hand, I did not find it particularly overly spicy. The breading I received was pretty bland, sort of like plain corn flakes but it let this marinade stand out. I used it again letting the chicken marinate for almost a week in the fridge and then cooked on the grill using a dry rub coating and now I will be using this one frequently.

Don't be scared. I did this on some chicken Maryland's. Marinated over night. Cooked on a wire rack brushing marinade over them ever 15min while cooking and turning once. The charred bits made everything even better. I didn't use onion powder. I ground fresh onion and ginger in a mortar and pestle and used a hot gochujang paste with lime juice. Flavours are spot on. I'm going to try it on pork next.

Halved recipie and added a little sesame oil and a tbsp chopped garlic. Didn’t have the peppers so added 1 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes to finish off the bottle. Came out quite spicy due to the extra pepper flakes but in a good way. Enough to marinate one chicken chopped into parts and skinned.

Delicious. chopped up chicken tenderloins and marinated overnight in portion sized baggies. Cooked one small batch with rice in my itaki lunch box and another small batch for dinner in a skillet with some of the marinade drizzled over it while it cooked. Came out even more delicious!

I added 3 cloves of crushed garlic and used red pepper flakes as a sub - took out a bit for sauce and added cornstarch to thicken it... Cut up some cutlets into smaller pieces, and baked it covered in the marinade for 45 minutes. And man - it's a winner.

Wife jarred the extra sauce almost immediately after tasting it, kids loved it too. Have those who don't like the heat avoid the sauce. 

Paired over white rice and steamed vegetables.
Add 2 tbsp of corn starch to thicken. Use chicken thighs or breasts.
Wow! Amazing! I added flour to the marinade to make the chicken crispy. I'm already planning to make this again.
Wow tastes amazing. I accidentally threw everything in at the beginning and used fresh chilli. Absolutely sensational.
It was really good - I used it on chicken thighs. I did not use all the sauce that I made, can it be frozen? - thx in advance

This marinade was delicious! Unfortunately I cut the sugar in half for the marinade, but since I only had to use 1/2 for the chicken, the other half I used for the sauce and I added back the sugar. Both the sauce and the chicken were full of flavor. I will definitely make this recipe again.
We made this to put on kabobs and oh my goodness it is delicious!! Definitely a recipe we’ll make again and again!
This marinade was yummy on bbq chicken
